sections.html:
The county offices share one address, 204 High Street in Marble Hill, Missouri 63764, and one main number, 573-238-1900. Say "Collector" for billing questions and "Assessor" for value questions.

Bollinger County offices at 204 High Street
OfficeLocation and phone
AssessorSuite 1, 573-238-1900 ext. 1
CollectorSuite 2, 573-238-1900
County ClerkSuite 5, 573-238-1900
RecorderSuite 7, 573-238-1900
TreasurerSuite 8, 573-238-1900

The courthouse is in Marble Hill, the county's one city. Glen Allen, Sedgewickville and Zalma are villages. The county is split among four school districts: Woodland R-IV at Marble Hill, Leopold R-III, Meadow Heights R-II at Patton and Zalma R-V.

Everything in Bollinger County is rural: 10,567 people in 2020, spread over 618 square miles of land. It sits within the Cape Girardeau metro area, and commutes average 35.5 minutes. Expect a small, local buyer pool of long-time owners, family transfers and people willing to drive.

  • Housing units in 2025: 5,045
  • Share of households that own, 2020-2024: 82.3 percent
  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $179,800
  • Median gross rent: $694
  • Building permits in 2025: 0

With so little new construction, existing houses carry the market. For those buyers, a clean tax record and a prompt, well-documented closing are what keep a contract together.

sections.h2: When Bollinger County taxes are due
sections.html:
December 31 is the last day in every Missouri county, Bollinger included. After it, unpaid balances start picking up interest and penalties, and RSMo 139.100 counts a mailed payment as timely when its postmark falls inside the period. For bill timing, accepted payment types and the current mailing address, call 573-238-1900 and ask for the Collector.

Land that stays unpaid is hit by RSMo 140.100, which adds an 18 percent penalty on that year's delinquency, or no more than 2 percent a month if the owner redeems ahead of a sale. Sales are held on the fourth Monday in August.

sections.h2: How the Bollinger County tax sale works
sections.html:
RSMo 140.150 puts land with unpaid taxes or special assessments up for sale on the fourth Monday of each August. Owners get several safeguards first.

  • Before delinquent land is published for sale, the collector sends a first class letter to the recorded owner.
  • If assessed value tops $1,000, a certified letter follows.
  • A certified letter returned unsigned triggers another first class letter, to the owner and any occupant.
  • Right up to the sale, you can clear the tax, penalty, interest and costs at the collector's office.

A notice that never reached you doesn't wipe out the tax. Moved recently? Give the Collector your new mailing address, since notices go to the owner of record.

Go first to the Assessor, Suite 1 at 204 High Street. The office values property annually and can explain what went into your number. Still disagree? The county Board of Equalization takes filings until the second Monday in July.

The state level is the Missouri State Tax Commission. RSMo 138.430 opens the next level, the Missouri State Tax Commission. Filing is due within the statutory time or 30 days after the board acts, whichever is later, and can be done online, by email, or by post to PO Box 146, Jefferson City, MO 65102. An attorney must file for any corporation, LLC, trust or estate.

You can contest value and still beat the payment deadline by paying under protest. Send the full amount by December 31 on a marked check, with a written statement for the Collector giving your claimed market value.

Bring the tax bill into the price talk early. Tax stays with the land, so whatever is unpaid passes to the buyer. The title company will usually run a tax search, but you can avoid surprises by phoning the Collector yourself to ask the balance and whether an earlier year is open.

If the Assessor holds the wrong mailing address, or the legal description on file differs from the deed, correct it before listing. Deed records live with the Recorder in Suite 7. The Treasurer in Suite 8 is not the Collector, so ask each office what it needs.

  1. Get the balance from the Collector, older years included.
  2. Correct any address or legal description error at the Assessor.
  3. Pass the payoff figure to the title company.
  4. Check that the Recorder will file the deed afterward.

A cash buyer runs the same tax search. With no lender in the picture, closing can go ahead as soon as the balance is cleared.

sections.h2: A Bollinger County calendar for sellers
sections.html:
The year repeats, so see where your sale falls.

  • Spring: value questions go to the Assessor first.
  • Second Monday in July: filing deadline for the Board of Equalization.
  • September 30: general State Tax Commission filing limit, unless the board ruled late.
  • Fourth Monday in August: tax sale of delinquent land.
  • December 31: payment deadline and postmark cutoff.

If you close in the fall, buyer and seller must decide who pays the bill that lands shortly before December 31. Write the answer into the contract, and ask the title company to hold the seller's share if no bill exists yet. Whoever pays should keep the receipt.

One short call to 573-238-1900 now prevents trouble later.

  • What do I owe on the parcel, and does any earlier year show a balance?
  • Which mailing address is on file?
  • Which payment types do you take, and what does each cost?
  • Has the parcel ever appeared on the August sale list?

Write down the answers and give them to the title company. A bill that is wrong because of value is the Assessor's problem to solve, not the Collector's.

On closing day the title company works from the balance the Collector gave you. If anything is owed for an earlier year, it comes out of your proceeds first, and the deed goes to the Recorder in Suite 7 after the papers are signed. Because the Recorder keeps the deed record, a clean filing is what puts the buyer's name on the books.

In a rural county with few sales, one open tax year can slow things down, since the buyer and the title company will want proof that nothing is headed for the August sale. Having your payment receipts and the Collector's written balance in hand answers that question quickly.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the tax payoff and the deed filing are often the only steps left once both sides sign. That makes it more important to settle any balance and address problems before the contract date.

Missouri's Property Tax Credit refunds up to $750 to older or disabled residents who paid real estate tax or rent and stay under income limits. Call the Department of Revenue at 573-751-3505 and file Form MO-PTC. To ask about any local senior freeze, call the County Clerk at 573-238-1900.

faqs.q: What is the Bollinger County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: December 31, the same as the rest of the state. Call 573-238-1900 and ask for the Collector to learn how and where to pay.

faqs.q: Where is the Bollinger County Assessor?
faqs.a: At 204 High Street, Suite 1, Marble Hill, MO 63764. The main number is 573-238-1900, extension 1 for the Assessor.

faqs.q: When is the Bollinger County tax sale?
faqs.a: The fourth Monday in August under state law, every year.

faqs.q: Can unpaid taxes be paid before the sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Under RSMo 140.150 you can pay the tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector right up until the sale.

faqs.q: How many people live in Bollinger County?
faqs.a: Roughly 10,646 in 2025, a 0.7 percent rise from 10,567 in 2020, across 618 square miles of land.
